post.name: post-install.sh
post.content:
#!/bin/sh
# Agama's "hostname"/"localization" profile properties aren't reliably
# applied by this installed Agama version (confirmed: hostname stayed blank,
# timezone stayed at the Europe/Berlin default) - set them directly instead,
# writing the config files systemd reads at boot rather than using
# hostnamectl/localectl, which need a running systemd/D-Bus not available
# inside this chroot.
echo "management" > /etc/hostname
ln -sf /usr/share/zoneinfo/America/Detroit /etc/localtime
echo "LANG=en_US.UTF-8" > /etc/locale.conf
echo "KEYMAP=us" > /etc/vconsole.conf

cat >> /etc/hosts <<'EOF'

# rke201-lab cluster
# IP_ADDRESS FQDN SHORT_NAME
172.30.170.2 	management.example.com		management
172.30.170.3 	server.example.com			server
172.30.170.4	agent.example.com 			agent
EOF

systemctl enable sshd

# "software.patterns" in the profile isn't applied either (confirmed via
# rpm -qa showing zero gnome packages after install) - same as
# hostname/localization, this installed Agama build doesn't wire it up.
# The explicit "gdm"/"gnome-session-wayland" packages above are the
# guaranteed-reliable fallback (software.packages does work), but also try
# the actual normal-install recipe here in case the install media's repo is
# still reachable at this post-install stage - if not, this is a harmless
# no-op and the explicit packages above still provide a working desktop.
zypper --non-interactive install --type pattern gnome_basic gnome gnome_x11 || true

# "systemctl set-default" may try to validate the target via systemd/D-Bus,
# which isn't running in this chroot (same constraint as hostnamectl above) -
# create the default.target symlink directly instead, matching how
# "systemctl enable" itself is just a symlink under the hood.
ln -sf /usr/lib/systemd/system/graphical.target /etc/systemd/system/default.target

mkdir -p /etc/sudoers.d
echo '%wheel ALL=(ALL) ALL' > /etc/sudoers.d/wheel
chmod 440 /etc/sudoers.d/wheel
